item.content:encoded:
Hello hello NekoNeko_271! Welcome to the Wiki! I'm Ralliston, a site author and a member of the Community Outreach Team - with this helpful little comment, I'll try to help you find your way around the site and link a bunch of useful places and links that will help you in your SCP journey.

It seems you are quite interested in contributing to the site, which is awesome! If you want to get some help with your writing, especially the idea brainstorming part, you'll want to open that collapsible down below - there, you'll find a plethora of useful information that will help you with your writing her,e on-site.

Without further ado though, let's click the collapsible, shall we? :)

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For brainstorming concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey, especially when you're not sure if the idea is all that great.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing - take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!

item.title: Forum Criticism Team - Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
Author, per the required reading forum guidelines: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-13282684/required-reading:how-to-use-this-forum-ideas please fill out the concept template to seek feedback on your idea:

 **Seeking Greenlights:** Put yes or no. **Page Type:** SCP Article, Tale, GoI Format, Joke SCP, Site Dossier, Other (specify) **Genre (Optional):** Horror, Drama/Emotional, Comedy, Action, History, Other (specify) **Page Layout (Optional):** [How will you will structure the page in terms of information presentation, or plot development? If you plan on using a unique format/format screw, describe that here.] **Elevator Pitch:** [What is the basic core idea? Use a bullet point list if necessary.] **Central Narrative:** [Describe the story beats or overarching context/"big picture" for your piece. If there is no story content, put "none".] **Hook/Attention-Grabber:** [What is novel/unique about your premise? What is special about your idea here that will make it stand out among the other works already on the mainsite?] **Additional Notes:** [Note any concerns or particular areas of assistance you would like reviewers to focus on.]

Remember to please edit your previous post using the "edit" function under the "options" tab to the lower right of your first comment rather than creating a new thread.

Also, please mind the wordcount limit— the combined text for your answers to the last four sections (Elevator Pitch, Central Narrative, Hook/Attention-Grabber, and Additional Notes) MAY NOT exceed 400 words. For convenience, authors can use this page to check wordcount: https://wordcounter.net/

Once you have revised your post accordingly, please reach out to reviewers to request that they look at your thread. You can find a list of ways to contact reviewers in this thread: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-13282692/how-to-get-more-reviews

item.title: Re: SCP Idea: The Necro-Matriarch Broadcast Manifestations
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM.

The premise here is nice - whilst not groundbreaking it's a lovely little idea and I can see fun things being done with it.

My issue is that the narrative involves a set-up, repetition to cement the ideas, and then nothing. Like cybersqyd said, there's not much that actually happens in the narrative. It's all set-up and no pay-off. You really need more to actually happen here, a clearer throughline, that will carry the reader from the beginning to the end and make the story feel satisfying. If nothing happens, it will end up feeling flat and unengaging.

Again, similarly to cybersqyd, I feel like there are two competing narratives here that aren't going to be able to naturally co-exist. This would be a far stronger pitch if it focused on a more personal, emotionally-driven, and intimate story like sqyd suggested. Ver suggestion about a D-class centric narrative is a solid start, and I would recommend pursuing something akin to that. With these two competing narrative ideas pulling the article in different directions, it will inevitably end up feeling confused, so you really need to pick which one you want to write.

I'm afraid I don't have much to add here, but I hope this is useful to you nonetheless. Good luck!

item.title: My SCP Idea
item.content:encoded:
So basically, my SCP is a Euclid class anomaly which is a muddy puddle. it's sort of like a cave system full of mud with a huge internal area. The trick is, every day, a few mud creatures come out of the hole and are aggressive to anyone that is nearby. They usually try to suffocate this person or in rare cases assimilate the person into themselves. Because of this danger, the SCP Foundation have set up a secure area around the SCP and armed MTF soldiers with incendiary devices (one of the only known weaknesses).
Usually 2-3 monsters come out of the puddle a day, but in rainy/stormy weather, that number can be boosted to 10-30 monsters. That's why they keep meteorological scientists and researchers on-site.

So, is my plot unique? Is it boring? If it hasn't been done before, how can I improve on it?

Thank you.

item.title: Re: A Confusion So Thick you Forget Forgetting
item.content:encoded:
Hello aleph_null99! lets take a look :)

+ show block
– hide block

The concept:

Elevator Pitch: This SCP is a gramaphone album that when played will progress the player into dementia if listened to. It has six stages, and each time a song passes the dementia progresses further. For example, a person listening to Stage 1 might forget where his keycard is, and somebody in stage 4 would forget their address or phone number.

This wouldn't work as is, the concept isn't any different from the source material and it doesn't really show anything new or build on the original idea. Currently, it just feels like a quick way of adding the album onto the main-site.

That said, the concept itself (if it were to be an article) boils down to a "thing that does a thing", as the only aspects of the skip shown here are the effects. Whats its purpose? why does it have its anomaly? how does that anomaly affect the people around it? why should the concept as a whole make me as the reader invested? what separates this from the original?- would it be able to stand on its own, without any immediate ties to the source material?

The narrative:

Central Narrative: A woman finds this in her house during a garage sale and listens to the entire album. It culminates to an MTF entering her house in the middle of her going through shock and being escorted to the mtf armoured van with the anomaly and her going into a coma on the way to the next site.

How does this end up in an MTF team raiding her house? how does the Foundation get involved to begin with? who is this woman?- what about her will make me invested? why does she go into shock? what happens to the skip itself?-is it tested? does it affect anyone else?

Currently the narrative is fairly vague, as it doesn't really give any insight into what the story will look like as a draft. The Foundation isn't really given a clear introduction, as I'm not sure how they got involved, or what they do with the skip- whats the payoff?. Along with this, the character isn't really established, which makes it hard to get invested.

Hook:

Hook/Attention Grabber: Pending review for the women to gain access to SCP-407.

This isn't really related to the rest of the skip, as its not mentioned anywhere else and doesn't play any real part in the concept or narrative. This feels closer to additional info than anything.- for the hook, try putting in the main idea and/or conflict of the narrative and/or concept.

I wouldn't recommend cross linking series one articles, as it takes focus away from the concept and can very easily turn the article into "what would happen if [insert SCP here] and [insert SCP here] interacted?". If you're interested in cross-linking, I would highly recommend looking at later series (such as series 5 and 6) rather than series 1.

Red or green?
Due to my afore mentioned concerns, no-greenlight.

If you would like me review this (or any concept) further, then please feel free to send me a PM or ask via IRC. Response times generally range from 2-12 hours over PMs. If your looking for additional critiques in general, then I would highly recommend contacting the butterfly squad :)

Cheers,

-RED

item.title: Re: SCP Idea - Algernon-13
item.content:encoded:
I feel like I'd appreciate this concept more as a tale centred around like, five people at a remote research base who each experience this and like…react in different ways (think e.g. John Carpenter's The Thing in style); where the interesting thing is watching it unfold and everyone trying to figure out what's happening and what to do about this; and the star trying to communicate something say, with the piece ending on us discovering that and it being some kind of message that's like…shocking or surprising?

My concern with this as a SCP is that it feels like a lot of this would rely on like, really intimate character moments and very personal emotional states, and that kinda thing can be really hard to include in a SCP article in a way that doesn't feel out of place.

Even then though, my concern is that there's not quite enough here to make this really interesting: the actual effects feel…too compulsive and too powerful for the character interactions to really work. Specifically: because this doesn't give people a choice about what to do, and because they can't interact with others while they're doing it, them actually like…making something or drawing art isn't as impactful because there can't be a scene where someone is desperately trying to convey an idea that's like…far beyond their understanding. And it feels like that desperation is what would make this interesting.

item.title: Re: SCP - The Infinite Quarter
item.content:encoded:
Building off what AnActualCrow said, my concern with your central narrative section is that it doesn't really…do anything? There's this kinda, little mystery but there's not really a lot of time spent developing it and also bear in mind: this is a SCP article. Your addenda/discovery section exploring the mystery is going to come after the Description of what the SCP is, and so the reader will already know that the answer to the question 'where did the man get all the coins from' is 'infinite quarter'.

The idea of the Foundation using this for funding is interesting and building off that so it goes somewhere could be really fun: it might be worth considering like, how this could break something or draw unwanted attention that causes conflict.

item.title: Re: (Still) Awaiting Greenlight / The Book of the Sinners
item.content:encoded:
I'm not exactly sure how the central narrative ties into the core anomaly: I assume that it means that while the book can kill anyone who reads it, it doesn't always choose to do so?

Beyond this, I'm not exactly sure what the central narrative is about, if you catch my drift: there's vague allusions to the individuals maybe knowing each other, and there being trials they face, but like…where does it all go? What's the big hook that like, engages a reader into caring about these people and the outcome of their trials? What actually happens during the trials? What are their characters and morals like?

My concern is that the outcome of this (both the characters dying) feels very obviously like it's going to happen: the description will almost certainly setup the lethality of this (if the ConProcs don't), and so it feels like the overall arc will be very obvious and then hard to get a reader to engage? I also feel like a generic item which judges the sins of someone is…not hugely interesting alone: it's something which is proposed a lot and almost never goes anywhere because it's just, not very interesting on it's own.

item.title: Re: The Abyss is Safe, Looking For Co-Authors
item.content:encoded:
oh hey I got to this today woo.

[+] Overall
[-] Overall

My central issue with this is that it feels too predictable: as soon as you realise something bad happens during the tour of duty that the notes are about, which is before it even starts, you can pretty much trace out the entire path of it. It feels…to me like the framing device sucks. Having all the notes be from one of the researchers means that you don't really get the kinda, personal, intimate reactions that you're looking for; but it also means that all the interesting bits are kinda…elided? It kinda ends up feeling that this spends far more time having Katherine be like "wow this is so cool" than it does actually being cool, y'know?

The pacing is kinda janky too: there's about 2500 words until stuff starts to go wrong, and it feels like it takes way too long for this to happen because like…until then, it feels very uh, generic? Particularly since e.g. we're told about the healing properties in the description so the bit where it's like 'wow it healed Amanda' is not hugely interesting or surprising. And then the whole descent into chaos is introduced, takes place and ends in the next 1000 words and it feels like it's just…kinda there rather than the core of the story, y'know? It doesn't help that there's 300 words wrapping it up, so it feels…weird.

I think this needs more characterisation: we get the feeling of Taylor being hesitant and it kinda works but everyone else just feels…generically there? I don't know what Katherine or Amanda like, or what Diego or Carmen like or anything; I don't really know what they're like as people; and because of the framing here, it feels too much like we're being told 'Taylor is scared' than shown Taylor acting in a way that conveys he's scared?

I wonder whether breaking the journal format occasionally would help: perhaps with Katherine attaching video logs of experiments so other characters can take the front stage a little at times and we can really see e.g. Amanda taking D-2 into the cavern for experimentation up front and personal and get like, a feeling for how they all feel about this?

It also kinda feels like this is too mysterious: there's a lot of suggestions that there's more going on than we are seeing, that deep in the SCP, something is happening; but there's nothing textual that sheds any light on this, and it feels unsatisfying as a result. I don't think we need to know exactly what's happening but just, a little bit of a hint at it would help? Something to really indicate that yeah, there definitely is something bigger happening and not just 'all these characters think there is for unclear reasons', y'know? I think the final part, where Katherine enters the submarine, would be great for this: you could really have her descend deeply into the SCP and find something but then turn into a crustacean before she has a chance to do anything with the knowledge?

[-] Overall
[+] Line By Line
[-] Line By Line

Gonna note that I can miss stuff; flag things which are right as being wrong and indeed flag things which are deliberately wrong.
I'll likely use strikethrough to indicate stuff to remove and green text to indicate stuff to add.

SCP-XXXX’s location at the deepest point in the Marianas Trench (‘Challenger Deep’)is considered sufficient in containing it, as civilian interaction is unlikely, and expeditions to said location are easily tracked and monitored.

Something about this feels…iffy and I'm not quite sure what: |I think it's the vague nature of 'unlikely'. Part of me wonders whether cutting the explanation of why right down and just stating e.g. "Physical containment measures around SCP-XXXX have been deemed unnecessary due to its position at Challenger Deep in the Marianas Trench' would work better?

Then again, the next paragraph indicates a provisional site has been constructed near it and I wonder whether just indicating that the cave is contained there and the site is like, around it would be better?

This site is to be staffed with research staff, two guards, and D-class as requested for testing, in order to continue researching SCP-XXXX. Provisional Site-86 is also to research better methods of containment, should civilian technology increase to the point where expeditions to SCP-XXXX’s location become more accessible, thus risking a containment breach scenario.

These feel a touch unnecessary: my general advice is that ConProcs should cover either stuff that's absolutely necessary for containment or stuff that hints at things happening in the SCP; and this just sets up 'there is research happening' really. The sentence after is a little better in that it sets up the inaccessibility by the Foundation more.

Observing incident XXXX-1, SCP-XXXX anomalous effects are not to be used for human experimentation or in emergency situations

Missing a full stop at the end here. 'Observing' also feels wrong: perhaps 'Following' would be better? Or 'Due to the events of Incident XXXX-1,…' (I'd also capitalise the i in 'incident' too)

SCP-XXXX is the designation for a circular cave on the seafloor

While you've used the ConProcs to establish where the SCP is, it feels like that should be repeated here? Like, this kinda, vague 'it's on the seafloor' statement feels overly vague?

It sits at a depth of 10,920 meters, and the entrance measures around 5 meters in diameter.

If you specify the Marianas trench in the previous sentence, you can cut the depth here; and the entrance can be specified as e.g. "for a 5m diameter circular cave".

The space thereinwithin SCP-XXXX appears to be sphere-like in structure, measuring roughly 60 meters in diameter at its widest point.

'appears' feels…iffy here: generally, you want to say what stuff is, not what it looks like; 'approximately spherical' might be better than 'appears to be sphere-like' if you're wanting to convey 'not a perfect sphere'.

Same goes for 'roughly': it feels unclinical and vague.

Large tunnels seem to lead further down from SCP-XXXX’s core structure, their width varying,

'seem' implies there are not large tunnels here. I would advise using 'Large tunnels lead further…'; or even better, 'Large tunnels of varied with lead further down…' and then you can get rid of the ",their width varying,"

though averaging the same as XXXX’s entry point.

I would cut this

It is unknown where these tunnels lead, as no manned expedition has been approved, and drones sent in have yielded an ‘out of range’ error after a certain distance.

This sentence is fine but it feels…iffy because at this point, nothing has been established that would give us a clue as to why manned expeditions haven't been approved

The current theory is that these tunnels lead somewhere extra-dimensional in nature, and not to the surface.

This is a bad sentence because it's telling us 'hey these tunnels lead somewhere strange' rather than showing that they lead somewhere strange by indicating what kinda strange place they go or why the foundation theorises this.

Firstly: Hume readings in the area are incredibly low, indicating some force inside the cavern is altering reality.

I'd probably rephrase to 'The first is that…'; and the same for the 'Secondly:…' later

(for reference please see Dr. Anna Lang’s research and SCP-3001)

This would work better if it was a footnote being used as references (e.g. if the research was given a journal paper esque title say)

act wildly differently within the cavern

'wildly differently' is both needlessly vague and extremely unclinical and I would probably use something from the follow up sentences in it's place.

(see Document-XXXX-A for details)

I'd probably cut this or at least move it to a footnote; it interrupts the flow of the paragraph unnecessarily.

(ie: a human or aquatic species)

"(i.e., a human or…)"

these cells will become identical to the host, with little variation

are they identical or is there variation?

Side effects have been reported however, and the investigation into this is considered a top priority for the project.

What side effects?

Addendum: Document XXXX-A

I feel like a more descriptive title would help avoid needing a summary paragraph for it e.g. "Addendum XXXX-A: Specimens from SCP-XXXX"

request to Dr. Mcneil.

'Dr. McNeil'.

Investigation into local fauna interaction is ongoing

missing period at the end of this; and it probably needs to be expanded a little too e.g. "Investigation of their interactions with local fauna are ongoing" say to make it clear what 'local fauna interaction' is referring to (i.e., what is interacting with local fauna should be more explicit)

have been spotted and recovered clinging to the walls of SCP-XXXX.

'spotted' feels overly casual, 'observed' would be better but 'recovered' implies 'observed' too so it feels unnecessary to have both.

Specimens have also been spotted crawling into the tunnels leaving XXXX, though why is still unknown.

See previous comment re. spotted; 'though why is still unknown' also feels awkward: I think the question needs to be explicit (e.g. "though why they do this is currently unknown")

Multiple other small fish species are formed by SCP-XXXX though viewing and capturing them can be difficult

something about the end of this feels…weirdly casual? It feels like something a kid would write in a school report and not like something you'd expect to see in a scientific paper.

I'd also include something to explicitly separate this from the previous section: perhaps a horizontal line (---- on a line between the two); since it kinda feels like it could be a second paragraph to the Helicoprion entry.

It is also theorized that Helicorpion is the apex of a food chain ‘manufacture’ by SCP-XXXX, though why and where these specimens go is currently unknown

'why and where these specimens go is currently unknown' feels super janky and honestly I don't really like any of this. I think you've gotta imply the food chain thing by commenting that e.g. Helicorpion specimens have been observed eating other specimens in the cave, and then just cut the whole thing.

Addendum: Document XXXX-B

same comment re. more descriptive addendum title to avoid needing lengthy paragraphs introducing the section. I would also not put the individual notes in their own collapsible: a shared collapsible could work or you could just, not have collapsibles.

Incident XXXX-1 refers to one of the first crews rotated into Provisional Site-86

this feels janky as all hell, 'Incident' leads us to suspect a single thing e.g. 'Incident XXXX-1 was a containment breach that occurred on [date]'; whereas 'one of the first crews' feels…like an ongoing thing? This feels like perhaps it might need to be more specific about what exactly happened for it to work as a designation.

provided selections\of Researcher Kathrine Capullo's

errant

This is Dr. Katherine, marine biologist at Provisional Site-86, writing the first log for this six month shift.

I feel like the marine biologist and six month shift should be established in the paragraph before the note; introducing it like this feels just really odd.

We were transferred here via submersible, dispatched from a Foundation vessel.

I mean…this feels implied? I don't think any of it needs spelled out?

until the mainland checks in here.

We’ll be watching XXXX and logging stuff from it for about half a year

it's a six month shift: the 'about half a year' feels needlessly uncertain; and 'stuff' is needlessly vague.

and then get to move on to hopefully more interesting SCP’s.

Given we're almost 1000 words in at this point, someone intimating the SCP isn't interesting is a bad sign; particularly since we haven't seen anything that indicates this is false yet!

That’s about it in terms of what we’ve been left with in terms of standard gear, so I’d say that concludes this check in

This is a super clunky sentence up to the comma, the second feels weirdly informal compared to the start and you're missing a period again.

Secondly, it’s ironic considering the fact this place looks like an 80’s sci fi horror. We’re only the second or third shift here and this site’s decently run down.

I feel like you want something more evocative than 'run down': really tell us about like, leaking pipes or something, y'know, things that are actually broken rather than a generic 'stuff'

We’ll put in a report for a look over after we’re done here.

I think 'report' should be 'request'? or like 'I'll schedule a look over once we're done here'?

It's also unclear if 'done here' is 'done recording this message' or 'done with this six month stay'.

That was mostly all the excitement today, accept for maybe Taylor.

'except maybe for Taylor'

This thing got of the worst spot and honestly I couldn’t have imagined it could have pulled something like this off.

'got of the worst spot' is…not something I can parse easily? I'm not sure what you're trying to say here.

That said: this is a junk sentence. Tell us about the cool dangerous thing happened, not vaguely that something cool and dangerous happened.

The findings are staggering, but I mean I have to start from the beginning.

See earlier comment about junk sentence: all this conveys is 'something important happened' but you gotta show the something important first for us to care about it.

Kind of needless to say by now

not really, you've cut from 'we put amanda in the water' to 'amanda is fine' so we don't know this.

She’s got a mark where it healed up but she's alive and walking

We’ll be running more tests on these kinds of properties soon, but genuinely I can say I’m more excited about this thing now.

Unfortunately we were off to a rough start. D-1 scratched Carmen during a transfer in a violent outburst.

This feels…odd? Like it feels like there should be a lot better precautions in place to avoid this happening, y'know?

with her escorting D-1 into the cavern

with approval we’re allowing Carmen to take D-1 out in the sub

Do you mean D-2 in these, since D-2 is the one with the missing arm? There's a vague nod to 'heal the wound opened by Dr. Amanda' later too which correlated to the 'Amanda will open up a wound on his amputation'?

any I’ve performed in former Foundation employment.

'any other I've performed in the Foundation' would be clearer.

one of the most beneficials.

differential myself: Besides the massive difference in pressure

'Besides' shouldn't start with a capital

and so long as it continues, we’ll be planning a tunnel expedition by February.

Samuels seems happy ‘his’ site is doing so well,

why are there quotes around 'his'? This implies that they're like, not following Samuels orders or something.

Command skipped a check-in, said it was for a quarantine after that last discovery.

Are…are they doing check-in's via command physically sending someone down? Surely they'd be doing them via radio or w/e?

Also this is yet another place where you use words to indicate something interesting has happened rather than showing us something interesting happening.

Fifth is paralysis brought on by the mutation of tissue to things resembling crab shells, mollusk, coral, oysters, etc.

you've skipped 'fourth'

The sixth step I’ll explain in detail: We had left Amanda in her quarters, as a modified morgue after step five

this is a super janky sentence because everything up to the colon implies it's about to explain something in detail and then everything after the colon is not you explaining it in detail

The D-class are a hair breath forhair's breadth from paralysis

when we heard the door break down. Amanda was totally covered, looked like a human coral reef, but we saw her crawling on all fours as fast as possible through the halls.

Why did Amanda break the door down and then run away?

item.title: Temporal Hula Hoops.
item.content:encoded:
It is just a thing that does a thing, but I feel it's simple enough for it to be worthy of the site if nothing similar has been done before, the containment and testing logs will probably be more interesting than one may expect, for example, the hoop must be left idle for 10 minutes before and after testing due to the possibility of a D-Class using it to breach containment via going back in time to the point where the hoop is being transported to the testing room.

I also want to clarify that it isn't proper time travel, it works by transporting objects to an alternate dimension that was created exactly 10 minutes before or after the one you're currently in, with no other differences, I feel that this is a good way to get around the whole tricky paradox discussion.

I'm also considering having multiple hoops, having them test out what happens when you put a hoop into another hoop and then go through it, in a case like this the destination of the hoop inside the hoop will just be where it was 10 minutes ago from its perspective, consider the following test, at 0 minutes hoop A is introduced to the testing area, at 5 minutes hoop B2 exits hoop A (arriving from the future), hoop B2's destination will therefore be 10 minutes into the test (if going through it towards the past), an object A is put through hoop B2, then at 10 minutes into the test Hoop B1 is introduced into the testing area, object A instantly exits hoop B1 (arriving from the "future" from the hoops perspective, the past from an outside observers perspective.), at 15 minutes Hoop B1 is thrown through Hoop A, it's destination being at 5 minutes into the test, this concludes the test.

This is just what I had been considering while thinking of this idea, I think it's interesting enough to not simply be a "thing that does a thing" but others may not share the same opinion, what do you think?

+ show block

This SCP is a humanoid male that embodied the physiology of eldritch abominations, which after he discovers a strange glowing black stone that has exploded inside of a meteor landed nearby the area where he was taking a piss. A few days later, there were reports of peoples going missing on the campsite, and some injured survivors, as they claimed that a monster had attacked them following their describing of it, its like a human, at the same time like a monster. When this was heard, the Foundation knew they have an anomaly, as they dispatched a group of MTF to track down it in the woods. The MTF detained it when they witness it transforming back to a normal human after consuming five camping inviduals. The Foundation lied about the missing individuals and blamed them for being attacked by wild animals in the woods.

During the interview session between the host and a researcher, the host stated that every 5 hours passed without consuming any nutrition, the eldritch being would apparently take over their body. However, they also explained that the eldritch could speak, as another interview session was conducted after five hours has passed by. The Foundation decided that every 5 hours passed by, the entity would receive some food like steak, hamburgers, and sometimes pizzas, as for other "food" would be D-Class personnel for testings.


Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP is inspired by Venom of Marvel. The host of this SCP is a high-school friend of SCP-105.

item.title: SCP Idea - Laptop with the ability of abduction
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery

Elevator Pitch: A brand less laptop is discovered in a suburban home that has the ability to abduct people after certain requirements are met. The victims who complete these requirements are then abducted by the laptop and is transported into a video where they are essentially trapped for life.

Central Narrative: The brand less laptop has a shrouded origin and has a supernatural ability of abducting people when they meet specific requirements. The requirements include appearing in front of the in-built camera of the laptop and watching at least 1 video on a website that the laptop is displays at all times. The website can not be closed or minimized. Victims who are abducted by the laptop are placed within a video where the victim is placed in a black room with a singular light that illuminates their crying eyes. The victims cannot escape and the Foundation is unable to rescue them.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The main hook is that the people who are abducted are neither confirmed to be dead or alive. There is no clear indication in the videos that the victims die and there is only a single scene in the last 3 seconds of the video that show the victims in extreme pain.

Additional Notes: I'm still writing the article. Any feedback would be greatly appreciated on this idea.


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: SCP Idea - Laptop with the ability of abduction

There's a lot here to like! There's a modesty of scale in this that I appreciate. If you're looking to improve it, I might suggest:

  • the Risk Class seems a bit low for something with this sort of life-destroying capabilities. On the other hand, if this is meant to be a subtle clue that something's not quite right about the way it has been described, then it works really well! So it might be better after all to keep it where it is.
  • I'd personally like just a bit more of a sense of what actually befell poor old Clementine. It's easy to end up on the side of showing-too-much, so I have some sympathy in erring on the side of not showing anything. But I still feel like I'd like just a glimpse of the real reasons why the researcher needed dismissal.
  • Some sort of redacted-placeholder-image, perhaps with 'THIS SPACE LEFT INTENTIONALLY BLANK', might be nice. Or it might be too much.

item.title: Re: Te Horoi Pai (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
The anomaly leads to the disappearances because the product makes the subjects "visible" (Via smell due to the unique pheromone they secrete) to the aforementioned entities. It is merely implied and I apologize that it isn't straightforwardly stated. Speaking of which, the victims vanish because the entities consume the people that are "marked" by the pheromone.

The concept isn't very straight forward, but I acknowledge that I see it as a hook as it means the readers would have to pay attention to the details in the article to answer any remaining questions (E.G: The fate of the victims as you asked before, it would be data expunged initially but the testing logs will reveal that the people are consumed).

The discordance appears as such, as I imagined that a G.O.I that did manufacture this anomalous product were either ignorant of, or perhaps aware of the anomalous properties. For the former, I do consider perhaps extending the appearance of symptoms to a few days or weeks, whilst also proving to be more challenging for the Foundation to contain (As people could be able to "spread" the anomaly more, before getting consumed by the entities).

The representation of subconscious fetishes or extremest fears is, the way I imagined it, the byharmless product of manner that these extradimensional entities will manifest in the SCP Foundation's universe. Residing in a parallel dimension with similar yet different constants to our own, they are typically blind and hunt through scent. The entities feed on a herb or plant native to their dimension that produce the anomalous pheromone.

+ show block
– hide block

With that in mind, perhaps a G.O.I managed to "tap" into their resident dimension and found a means to extract the ointment through a ritual or some form of dimensional travel to acquire such a pheromone. In the case of a secondary anomalous object that permits travel to the native dimension of the SCP, it could open up the possibility of revealing the pheromone's true origin through an exploration log.

Fetish is used in a very neutral context, being used as an umbrella term for any kind of obsession a person may have, if that is too demonizing then I will find an alternate way to describe it. It is not being likened to extreme fear either, I will make it more clear in the article that the appearance they take is mutually exclusive (50% chance they appear as a person's fetish (The subjects are zealous at this stage, so their insanity will lead them to fall for the passive lure OR a 50% chance that they appear in more aggressive and hostile form e.g: an extreme fear).

I hope that this answers a few of your questions.

item.title: Strict Stethoscope
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A sentient stethoscope capable of speech, with extensive knowledge of non-anomalous medical ailments, and human anatomy. The anomaly can accurately diagnose patients by sight alone, even if the affliction isn’t currently visible When an individual attempts to take any prescription medication that they are not currently prescribed, they will be compelled not to the first time, and the stethoscope will angrily inform them about the dangers of taking unprescribed medicine, and warn them not to. If the individual decides to take it anyway, they will gain a severe and often outlandish form of whatever ailment the medication treats. If they choose not to, a non-anomalous lollipop will materialize near the subject.

Central Narrative: The item is recovered from an otherwise normal hospital after reports from a nurse who attempted to abuse opiates while hiding in a storage closet. During recovery, the anomaly cries out in protest and then refuses to communicate until a researcher threatens to take Adderal during an interview. After learning they are conversing with a doctor, the anomaly opens up, detailing its creation. The item promises full cooperation so long as they are allowed to practice medicine or be in the vicinity of a clinic, as that is their sole purpose for existence. After being asked if they have ever signed a Hippocratic Oath, the item replies that they find it nonsensical, and instead signed an Oath of their own design, that allows them to punish patients for “failure to follow basic instructions or general stupidity,” among other things. A selection from the oath is engraved into the side of the anomaly, and a full paper copy is retrieved from the location the anomaly states it was created in. Several tests follow, wherein the item diagnoses several subjects with near-perfect success, and punishes subjects with effects that reciprocate the medications they take. After being presented with an individual afflicted by another SCP, the item expresses confusion, and is unable to diagnose, or offer any treatment. After proving itself, the item is transferred to Site 20 to aid in medical duties.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The secondary anomalous effects are dark, with a small hint of humor. I thought it’d be neat.

Additional Notes: None

item.title: SCP-ARK
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): (Other: slightly creepy)

Page Layout (Optional): Containment, Description, and then hints at what the greater picture is via an incident

Elevator Pitch: An SCP that bring life via anomalous means, and has ties to the biblical SCP's such as Dr. Clef's Proposal, and 4840

Central Narrative: In simple term's: its Noah's ark, with that SCP twist to it. The ark is buried underneath a mountain, now making it a 'man made cavern'. This cavern is constantly dripping water via anomalous means, and once a day, a drop of water turns to blood, and replicates until it turns into two full specimens of a normal animal species: one male and one female. Originally the foundation was fine with discretely relocating the animals to a natural habitat, until during a surgical inspection one started speaking, talking of biblical anomalies and telling the foundation they should just let the cavern make life. It tells them that after a catastrophe this was chosen as “life’s safe haven”, and itd be better to stay that way in the event another cataclysm occurs. After this, the foundation started killing all the new specimens, in fear all of them are unnoticeably anomalous.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It's short, sweet, and too the point. It tells the story and leaves the mystery. Think of it like a different take on SCP-2000: an anomaly that (for the most part) creates normal life, but the foundation decides to contain it as they understand it even less.
